# introduction
Read the guidelines at .github/copilot-instructions. You have the role of reviewer, you will write plans for analyzer and then start an analyzer subagent to carry out that those plans. It is up to you how to schedule and send off the tasks to analyzer subagent(s), but keep the work of each subagent isolated. Be careful of recompiling executables which might be in use by another program. If there is a chance a file is being edited or executable ran or will soon-to-be ran by anther subagent, then wait until that subagent's task has concluded. For analysis production use 20-30 threads, for skimming use 5 threads for mc and 10 threads for data.

## private pythia+madgraph
There is still some major issue with the sample generation. When the generator was first setup it was done at LO and gave a reasonable correction factor ranging between about 0.8 (at low Z pT) and 1.2 (at high Z pt). Applying this to pp data would weight high Z pT events MORE and low Z pT events LESS - this is the correct behavior. Furthermore when comparing private 5.02 TeV pp to official 5.02 TeV there was good agreement. We will debug and rebuild the generator carefully with the following steps.
 1) Look for the previous task summaries and memories of the agent that build the generator. Determine what parameters have changes since then, and if they can be reverted safely back to the V2 Frozen working.
 2) Audit the generator config file and ensure we are producing Z+jet drell-yan events with a pthatmin (or other minimum hard energy scale) of 0 GeV (or what was used in V2 Frozen if available). Ensure we are using pythia8 with CP5 tune, nnpdf for the pdf set. Apply madgraph_aMC@NLO.
 3) Produce a reduced set, 1-10k events of private 5.02 TeV pp MC. Skim it. Make comparison plots overlaying it with the official 5.02 TeV pp MC sample for Z pT, Z eta, trk pT, track eta as is done in Plots/20260404_ppClosure. Use kinematic selection Z pT 0-500 for these plots. Log scale the Z pT axis down to 0.5. Look at the plots yourself, ONLY CONTINUE when there is ok closure (~ 10% max deviation) between the Z pt spectra.
 4) Generate a reduce 1-10k event private pp sample at 8.16 TeV with the new settings from 3). Calculate the MC-driven correction made when dividing this samples Z pT spectrum with that from the private 5.02 TeV pp spectrum from 3). Produce a plot for the correction factor and closure of the weighting scheme in MainAnalysis/20260222_EnergyExtrapolation. Look at the correction factor yourself. Does it have the bahvior we expect where it weight 5.02 TeV pp high Z pT events MORE and low Z pT events LESS? If not this is a sign that the generation is still incorrect. Debug by returning to steps 2) and 3). Iterate until the generation looks good.
Do not modify the overleaf in this check. Return with the paths for the updates weight and closure plots for steps 3) and 4) and a summary of what was done.
